titulo: Subjunctive or indicative after tal vez and quizás
subtitulo: Tal vez vaya / tal vez voy: both work, but not at the end of the sentence.
regla: Tal vez, quizás, quizá (maybe) take the indicative or the subjunctive. Present or future doubt: present indicative or subjunctive. At the end of the sentence: only indicative.

bloques.texto: **Tal vez**, **quizás** and **quizá** mean _maybe, perhaps_. They express probability or doubt, and they can be followed by the **indicative** or the **subjunctive**.
The subjunctive usually sounds a bit more doubtful; the indicative a bit more likely. Both are correct.

filas: Quizá no aprobó. / Quizá no ha aprobado.
Quizá no haya aprobado. / Quizá no aprobara.

bloques.texto: **Placement:** if **tal vez** or **quizás** goes at the **end** of the sentence, only the **indicative** is possible: **No aprobó, tal vez.** ✓ **No haya aprobado, tal vez.** ✗
Tip: maybe-words open the door to both moods, but only from the front.

lista.es: No sé qué me pasa; quizás ==estoy== un poco nervioso.
lista.en: I don't know what's wrong with me; maybe I'm a bit nervous.

lista.es: No sé qué me pasa; quizás ==esté== un poco nervioso.
lista.en: I don't know what's wrong with me; maybe I'm a bit nervous.
I might go to the concert today.

lista.es: Tal vez ==vaya== a la playa mañana.
lista.en: I may go to the beach tomorrow.

lista.es: Quizá Beto no ==haya pasado== el examen.
lista.en: Maybe Beto didn't pass the exam.

lista.es: Beto no pasó el examen, ==tal vez==.
lista.en: Beto didn't pass the exam, maybe.

lista.texto: In Mexico, **a lo mejor** (always indicative) is very common: **a lo mejor voy**.

bloques.texto: Say it out loud, then open the answer.

lista.p: Say it two ways: _Maybe I'll go to Rosarito._ (tal vez)
lista.r: Tal vez voy a Rosarito. / Tal vez vaya a Rosarito.

lista.p: Which one is wrong? **Tal vez llueva.** / **Llueva, tal vez.**
